main_text.p: Mathematica, quæ fit secundùm rationem, sed non II. Mathema-tica. secundùm rem: ut triangulum consideratur non phy-sicè, quatenus est ligneum, aureum: sed abstractè. Abstrahi autem non potest secundùm rem, sed solum-modò secundùm rationem. Deniq; sunt alia entia separata secundùm esse & intellectum à motu & materiâ sensibili. Atq; hinc est abstractio Metaphy-III. Metapysi-ca. sica, quæ fit secundùm rationem & rem. Sic unitas à Metaphysico considerat abstracta, & secundùm rationem, & secundùm rem. Joan. Jandun. in procem. in lib. de anim. Caterùm illud ipsum phantasma corporeâ crassitudine exutum intelle-ctus agens devehit ad patientem, in quo gignitur actus sciendi, dum intellectus patiens imaginem receptam judicat. Hinc res, quatenus intelligibilis, dicitur objectum intellectus agentis; quatenus intellecta, intellectus patientis. Quum autem intellectus agens se conjungit cum patiente, dicitur intellectus adeptus.

V. Voluntas operatur circa id quod concepit intellectus. Ejus objectum est [?]βαλητὸν[?], seu ἐφετὸν[?]: est q; tantum bonum, sive sit tale καθ' ἀλήθειαν[?], sive κατὰ δόξαν[?]. Sic quando aliquis furatur, non vult malum formaliter, sed malum concipit sub ratione boni. Voluntatis actus duplex, præeligere, & elige-Voluntatis actus du-plex. re, id est, velle propter se, & velle propter aliud.

p.i: Præeligit & per se vult finem, eligit media ad finem, & propter finem.

main_text.p: VI. Memoria intellectiva, & recondit ea, quæ intellectu atq; voluntate sunt comprehensa, & ubi opus fit, eadem promit. Exemplum cupis? Habes hoc: Veritatis de Christo confessio. Ad

page.notes: Long s is printed as a sign like s and is transcribed as plain s throughout. "Deniq;" and "Atq;" use a superscript sign after q that is not clearly legible; copied as q; with the sign read as a standard abbreviation, so check against the scan. The Greek words in the fifth paragraph are rendered from a small, blurred print: the first ([?]βαλητὸν) and the accents are uncertain, and so are the words καθ' ἀλήθειαν and κατὰ δόξαν. The word after "Ha-" at the line end ("befis") is doubtful; read as "besis" with [?]. In the last line, "Ad" stands on the same line as the text and is read as text, not as a catchword. Two of the line-end hyphens ("phy-", "elige-") were preserved as printed. The margin notes "II." and "III." are roman numerals beside the notes and are kept inside them.
